A1.justification: Despite the changed title and emphasis, both PDFs describe the same PAWS-based research framework. Their complete main texts and supplements support matching the methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, pretraining, prototype-selection, transfer-learning and RoPAWS experiments, including supplementary sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments and additional OOD detection, component-ablation and embedding analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The pseudolabel target changes from a sharpened geometric combination of predictions in v1 Equation 21 to a sharpened arithmetic average in v2 Equation 9. v2 also specifies maximum prototype cosine similarity for OOD scoring. These are limited procedural changes; the overall frozen-backbone/projector design, vMF-SNE pretraining and k-means selection procedure remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds OOD detection around CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, using Tiny ImageNet and the opposite CIFAR dataset for near OOD, and Places365, DTD, MNIST and SVHN for far OOD. The seven original classification datasets, binary DeepWeeds task and cross-dataset pretraining coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds +SemiReward and Semi-ViT comparisons and drops v1 Table 2's CIFAR-100 comparison attributed to Shrinking Class Space. The new OOD comparison includes DeepEnsemble, KNN, CIDER, LogitNorm, PixMix and PALM. USL also gains reported Food-101 comparisons, which v1 left unreported.

E3.justification: v2 expands model settings from DINOv2 ViT-S/14 to include ViT-B/14 and ViT-L/14. It introduces near/far OpenOOD evaluation with AUROC and FPR reporting and a Gaussian-kernel control. The original classification label budgets, stated splits, and 50-epoch training/20-epoch pretraining budgets remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds OOD component ablations, backbone-versus-projection OOD comparisons, and embedding/density analyses in Figures 4–6. Head/loss ablations expand to CIFAR-100 and Food-101. The original hyperparameter study becomes Table S6, adding those datasets and a Gaussian-kernel comparison. Transfer-learning and RoPAWS studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run means and standard deviations, 20-run prototype-diversity plots with minimum/maximum bars, and mainly single-run nondefault hyperparameter tests. No new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is specified. Additional result rows and changed uncertainty values do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds OOD and larger-backbone results and revises retained classification, transfer, RoPAWS and kNN entries. For example, the modified method's CIFAR-100 result changes from 73.6±1.2 in v1 Table 2 to 75.7±0.9 in v2 Table 3 alongside the loss revision. USL/SKMPS means reverse order: 76.3/76.6 in v1 Table 3 versus 77.5/77.3 in v2 Table 4. Larger-model headline accuracies are not same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The formal multiview target and loss definition changes between v1 Equations 21–22 and v2 Equation 9. v1's explicit Gaussian/Student-t SNE and distillation derivations are also removed. The central PAWS probability derivation and vMF-SNE construction remain substantially unchanged, with no new theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims improvements to PAWS/RoPAWS and few-label classification. v2 presents PAWS-VMK as a joint SSL/OOD approach competitive with specialized detectors, making OOD detection central to the title, abstract and introduction. This capability was only proposed for future investigation in v1's discussion.

C2.justification: v2 introduces explanations linking the components to compact prototype clusters, improved class separation and OOD detection. Appendix A interprets backbone-versus-projection differences through DINOv2's pretraining exposure, while Appendix B identifies dataset-dependent hyperparameter preferences. v1's speculative distillation, adversarial-robustness and multimodal-LLM discussion is removed. The retained blanket SKMPS superiority wording is less consistent with v2 Table 4's CIFAR-100 ordering.

D1.justification: v2 adds GPU memory capacity and timing information for larger backbones while retaining most implementation details and hyperparameter tables in Appendices C–D. It omits v1's explicit best-validation-epoch/test-reporting rule and Food-101 run-exclusion explanation. The PDFs do not explain how the previously excluded USL Food-101 runs became reportable.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts toward the intersection of SSL and OOD detection, with substantial new coverage including OpenOOD, PALM, SemiReward and several OOD comparison methods. CIDER, already cited prospectively in v1, becomes a central comparator. The earlier emphasis on biological concept learning and knowledge distillation is removed or reduced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and discussion are substantially rewritten around OOD detection. PAWS background moves into methodological preliminaries, and several original main-text studies move into reorganized appendices. PAWS-VM/VMK and SKMPS terminology accompanies this broader narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 changes from a two-column to a single-column format and adds a framework diagram, OOD tables and embedding/density figures. Original Figure 2 is split between an expanded main-text ablation figure and supplementary training curves. Several tables move to the supplement, and the hyperparameter tables are spread across multiple pages.

improvement.justification: The Gaussian-kernel control, broader sensitivity tests and additional component ablations substantially strengthen support for the design choices. OOD experiments replace v1's speculation with benchmark, component and backbone comparisons, making applicability more assessable. These gains outweigh the unexplained Food-101 reporting change and overly broad SKMPS superiority wording, although those issues limit reproducibility and claim precision.
